output.summary: Cumulative alpha is +0.85% over 8 weeks with a 37.5% weekly win rate — barely beating a falling SPY, mostly on the back of one MU winner (+33.4%) that offset a string of high-conviction chases (MSFT -11.8%, AVGO -14.5%, SMCI -12.9%, NVDA-add -10.1%). Recent 3 weeks have flipped negative on alpha as the rotation trades (XLF/XLI/V/JPM/BRK.B) deliver only market-like returns while entry sizing has been mediocre.
what_worked: Cutting broken theses fast: closing MU on the $47.8M cluster sale (6/29–7/06) and AVGO/SMCI TLH on 6/15 avoided further drawdown — the insider-cluster hard-rule is earning its keep.
Sizing up the cleanest cross-signal MU (5/25 high conviction) delivered +33.4% and single-handedly rescued cumulative alpha — 'concentrate don't sprinkle' worked when signals were unambiguous.
Respecting wash-sale and macro_mismatch hard rules (XLP/XLU/XLE avoids in expansion regime) prevented adding to defensive drags.
Alpha positive in down weeks (6/22 +1.38%, 6/29 +0.54%) — the cyclical/quality tilt is genuinely defensive when SPY sells off.
what_missed: High-conviction OPENs at extension keep losing: MSFT 6/01 (RSI extended, -11.8%), AVGO 6/01 (-14.5%), SMCI 5/25 (tech 91 chase, -12.9%), NVDA-add 5/25 into 6.0 weight (-10.1%). Pattern: technical ≥80 + news ≥90 at entry = mean-reversion trap, not breakout.

Rotation ETF sleeve (XLF/XLI/DIA/IWM added 6/15–6/29) is producing near-zero alpha — 'diversify into cleaner ETFs' has diluted returns without cutting risk meaningfully. Basket weighted return -0.94% vs equal-weight -0.47% suggests larger positions are underperforming smaller ones.
Cold-start basket 5/18 (XLE, BRK.B, GOOGL, NVDA, AMZN) all closed red between -0.5% and -12.9% — diversification without edge is just index-hugging with worse fees.
AAPL 6/08 WWDC-catalyst open (-6.0% in a week) confirmed the reflection warning against buying overbought RSI into a known event.
lessons_for_pm: Hard rule: do NOT OPEN when RSI≥70 AND news polarity≥0.90 — last 4 instances (MSFT, AVGO, SMCI, AAPL) averaged -10.6%. That's exit liquidity, not a breakout.

Concentration works only with a genuine cross-signal edge. If you're opening 3+ new ETF positions in a week (like 6/15 and 7/06), you're diversifying because you lack conviction — either take one meaningful position or hold cash.
MU is the template: sentiment 94 + technical 82 + macro_fit and NOT stretched at entry (RSI mid-range). Look for that specific profile before sizing >5%.
Follow through on insider-cluster exits without hesitation — MU close (7/06) after -11.6% week validated the rule; don't wait for a second confirming week next time.

Basket weighted return (-0.94%) is worse than equal-weight (-0.47%), meaning our sizing decisions are actively hurting. Bias new opens smaller (4-6% not 8-10%) until win rate on high-conviction OPENs improves above 50% (currently 50% at 10 picks but skewed by MU).
Cash is a position. With current 42% pick win rate, reflexively deploying to 100% is negative expected value — hold 15-25% cash unless a cross-signal alignment matches the MU template.
watch_for: This week's JPM/BRK.B/XLV opens (7/06) are still fresh — check whether they're extending on RSI or basing; if RSI already >65, don't add.
Bank earnings this week (JPM print) — if XLF has already run into it, the reflection pattern says fade the news, don't chase it.
Concentration in cyclicals (XLI ~9.5% + XLF ~10% + JPM 10% + DIA + IWM) is now ~40% of book in one macro trade — a rotation reversal would hit hard. Consider one non-correlated ballast slot.
